walkthroughs.body_html:
International Relations: Changing Superpower Relations 1941-2010 — a core area of GCSE History.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

International Relations: Changing Superpower Relations 1941-2010 brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with International Relations: Changing Superpower Relations 1941-2010.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

Why did Japan attack Pearl Harbor?
options: Japan attacked because it wanted to conquer America.
William was Edward the Confessor's eldest son.
To cripple the US Pacific Fleet and buy time to secure resource-rich Southeast Asia after the US oil embargo threatened Japanese expansion.
Japan attacked to support Germany's invasion of the USSR.

mcqs.q: When did the systematic mass murder of Jews begin?
options: Mass shootings by Einsatzgruppen began with Operation Barbarossa in June 1941; industrial extermination camps followed from 1942.
The killings only began after Germany lost the Battle of Stalingrad.
William was Edward the Confessor's eldest son.
The Holocaust began as soon as Hitler came to power in 1933.
